In all cases whatever number is formed using six {1}^{'}$ or six {8}^{'}$s or three {1}^{'}$s + three {8}^{'}$s, that number can be splited into sum of multiples of $1001,1008,8001,8008$ (all of them are divisible by $7$). So, all the numbers thus formed will be divisible by $21$,

questions.question: Let $A,B$ and $C$ be three events such that the probability that exactly one of $A$ and $B$ occurs is $(1 - k),$ the probability that exactly one of $B$ and $C$ occurs is $(1 - 2k),$ the probability that exactly one of $C$ and $A$ occurs is $(1 - k)$ and the probability of all $A,B$ and $C$ occur simultaneously is {k}^{2},$ where $0 < k < 1.$ Then the probability that at least one of $A,B$ and $C$ occur is:

Adding $\left(i\right),\left(ii\right) & \left(iii\right)$, we get

$P\left(A\right) + P\left(B\right) + P\left(C\right) - P\left(A \cap B\right) - P\left(B \cap C\right) - P\left(C \cap A\right) = \frac{ - 4k + 3}{2}$

$P\left(A \cup B \cup C\right) = P\left(A\right) + P\left(B\right) + P\left(C\right) - P\left(A \cap B\right) - P\left(B \cap C\right) - P\left(C \cap A\right) + P\left(A \cap B \cap C\right) \implies P\left(A \cup B \cup C\right) = \frac{ - 4k + 3}{2} + {k}^{2} \implies P\left(A \cup B \cup C\right) = \frac{2{k}^{2} - 4k + 3}{2} \implies P\left(A \cup B \cup C\right) = \frac{2(k - 1{)}^{2} + 1}{2} \implies P\left(A \cup B \cup C\right) = {\left(k - 1\right)}^{2} + \frac{1}{2} \implies P(A \cup B \cup C) > \frac{1}{2}$

questions.question: An unbiased coin is tossed. If the outcome is a head then a pair of unbiased dice is rolled and the sum of the numbers obtained on them is noted. questions.explanation:
Let, $A$ be the event that the noted number is either $7$ or $8.$

And, {E}_{1}$ be the event that the toss of coin results in head and {E}_{2}$ be the event that the toss of coin results in tail.

Then, we have $P\left({E}_{1}\right) = P\left({E}_{2}\right) = \frac{1}{2}$

And, $P\left(A | {E}_{1}\right) = P($getting the sum of the numbers on the pair of dice as $7$ or $8)$

The total number of cases, when a pair of dice is thrown are $= 6 \times 6 = 36$ and the cases of getting sum $7$ or $8$ are $\left(\left(1,6\right),\left(2,5\right),\left(3,4\right),\left(4,3\right),\left(5,2\right),\left(6,1\right),\left(2,6\right),\left(3,5\right),\left(4,4\right),\left(5,3\right),\left(6,2\right)\right) = 11$ cases.

$\implies P\left(A | {E}_{1}\right) = \frac{11}{36}$

Similarly, $P\left(A | {E}_{2}\right) = ($getting the number $7$ or $8$ from the numbers $1,2,3,..,9) \implies P\left(A | {E}_{2}\right) = \frac{2}{9}$

Now, using the total probability theorem, we get

$P\left(A\right) = P\left({E}_{1}\right)P\left(A | {E}_{1}\right) + P\left({E}_{1}\right)P\left(A | {E}_{2}\right) \implies P\left(A\right) = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{11}{36} + \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{2}{9} \implies P\left(A\right) = \frac{11}{72} + \frac{1}{9} = \frac{19}{72}.$

Or

$\begin{matrix}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ evenplace & oddplace & evenplace & oddplace\end{matrix}$

Thus, the required probability is $\left(\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{3} \cdot \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{2}{3}\right) + \left(\frac{2}{3} \cdot \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{3} \cdot \frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{1}{18} + \frac{1}{18} = \frac{1}{9}.$

Probability of success i.e. getting a $5$ or $6 = P\left(s\right) = \frac{2}{6} = \frac{1}{3}$.

$\implies X = 100 \implies P\left(X = 100\right) = \frac{1}{3}$

Case II : First throw is other than $5$ or $6$ and second and third throws are $5$ or $6$, game stops

$\implies X = 50 \implies P\left(X = 50\right) = \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{1}{3} = \frac{2}{9}$
